newsitem.title: USA: Revolutionary bellows design wins student award.
newsitem.headline: Revolutionary bellows design wins student award.

text.p: A graduate student at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology won a $30,000 prize on Tuesday for revolutionising the ancient shape of bellows with a few simple folds of material.
For his design and other inventions, Nathan Kane, 28, from Austin, Texas, was awarded the 1997 Lemelson-MIT Student Prize for inventiveness.

"They've been around for thousands of years. Who would change bellows?" professor Sanjay Sarma told a news conference. "Nathan has single-handedly pushed the state of the art in bellows for the first time in, I don't know, thousands of years."
By adding extra folds, Kane enabled bellows to extend two to three times as far with the same material. His design also eliminated a bulky support structure, making them lighter.
Kane said he was talking with a company to license the design for commercial purposes.
